title: Five jobs,
one window.
jobs.lead: The launcher is the whole player side of OPEN//77. You do not install anything into your game folder by hand, and you do not edit a config to join a server.

items.title: Signs you in
items.body: One OPEN//77 account, authorized in your browser rather than in the app. The launcher never sees your password.

items.title: Checks your game
items.body: It makes sure your Cyberpunk 2077 install is build {build} with {expansion} before it installs anything. The client is built against that exact version, so you hear about a mismatch up front rather than halfway into a session.

items.title: Installs and updates the mod
items.body: The OPEN//77 client is fetched, verified and kept current for you. Nothing to unzip into your game folder by hand, and nothing left behind when you turn it off.

items.title: Manages what loads
items.body: Choose which mods are active for a session. Some servers ask for a clean load-out, so this is how you keep your own setup and still connect.

items.title: Finds you a world
items.body: Browse community servers, filter them, and press connect. The launcher starts the game already pointed at the world you picked.

firstRun.title: What actually happens.
firstRun.lead: Already installed? Open the launcher, pick a server and press connect. It takes care of the rest.

steps.title: Windows will show a warning
steps.body: The launcher is not code-signed yet, so the first launch brings up SmartScreen’s “Windows protected your PC” screen. Choose More info, then Run anyway, and you are through. Windows shows that message for every unsigned application, plenty of indie launchers included, and it says nothing about the file itself. The launcher guide spells out exactly what that dialog does and does not mean.

steps.title: Sign in through your browser
steps.body: The launcher opens <authorize>the authorization page</authorize> on this site. You approve it there, and the launcher receives a token. Your password never goes through the app.

steps.title: Point it at your game, then play
steps.body: It locates your Cyberpunk 2077 install, checks the build, installs the client, and opens the <servers>server browser</servers>. From there it is one button.

requirements.title: What you need.

items.title: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit
items.body: The launcher is a Windows desktop application, and the client it installs is a native plugin that loads inside the game process. There is no macOS or Linux player build.

items.title: Your own copy of Cyberpunk 2077 {build}
items.body: Your own legal copy: OPEN//77 never distributes the game or any of its assets. The build has to be {build} exactly, not a minimum: the client hooks the engine at addresses established for that build, and the launcher checks it for you.

items.title: {expansion}
items.body: Required rather than optional: the world you land in when you connect is an EP1 save, so there is nothing to load without it.

faq.a: Expected: the launcher is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen flags it like every unsigned application. Choose More info, then Run anyway. Only run the copy you got from this page, and if you want to be sure it is the same file, compare its SHA-256 under “File details & verification” above. The launcher guide explains the dialog in full.

faq.q: Why are the launcher and server versions different?
faq.a: They are separate release channels. The Windows button above always serves the current launcher; <host>the server page</host> serves the current dedicated server. Neither substitutes an older build when the other is unavailable.

faq.q: I want to host, not play.
faq.a: Hosting is a different download. A dedicated server never needs Cyberpunk 2077 installed and does not use this launcher. Start at <create>Create a Server</create>, then <host>download the server</host>. The archives are public; a free account with a verified email lets you create its license key.

faq.q: Do I need to apply before playing?
faq.a: No. Open Alpha is available to everyone. Download the launcher, sign in with your free OPEN//77 account and join a community server. Read the <alpha>Open Alpha guide</alpha> for setup and requirements.

requirements.alphaTitle: This is Alpha software, not a stable release.
requirements.alphaBody: Expect bugs, crashes, incomplete features and updates that change APIs. The <discord>Discord</discord> is where you can get help, report reproducible issues, meet other creators and follow the changelog.

experiences.lead: OPEN//77 doesn’t ship a game mode. It ships the platform. A hardcore roleplay city, a ranked racing league, a survival district, a social hub with zero combat, or something nobody has built yet: they’re all just servers.

items.title: A dedicated, persistent world
items.body: Your server keeps running when players log off. Economies, factions and stories continue. The world remembers, because you host it.

items.title: Your rules & moderation
items.body: Whitelist or open door, hardcore or casual: you set the rules, pick the staff, and shape the culture of your community.

items.title: Custom gameplay & resources
items.body: Add jobs, economies, missions, vehicles and UI through resources, drop-in packages of gameplay. Use what the community shares, or script your own.

items.title: A front door for your community
items.body: Your server page in the public browser shows your world, mode, language and player count. Discovery is built into the platform.

how.title: Three steps to open the doors.

steps.title: Get the server
steps.body: Download the <host>dedicated server software</host> and run it on your own hardware or a rented machine. It is a normal server process: it does not need Cyberpunk 2077 installed, and you own it entirely.

steps.title: License it to your account
steps.body: Create a free account, mint a license key in the <keys>keymaster</keys>, and put it in your server config. The key ties the server to you and is what the master checks before it lets the server onto the platform.

steps.title: Open the doors
steps.body: Shape your slots, rules, language and mode, add the resources you want, and your licensed server appears in the public browser. Players’ clients auto-download everything your world needs.

how.notice: Every server on the platform belongs to an account. The <licensing>server licensing guide</licensing> walks through creating an account, getting a license key, and linking it to your server so the master authorises it. See also the <requirements>platform requirements</requirements>.

start.title: From download to open doors.
start.lead: The same four steps for a local test server and a public one. Start with the included Freeroam, then make it yours.

steps.title: Mint a license key
steps.body: Create one in the <keys>keymaster</keys>. It ties the server to your account and is shown once, so keep it somewhere safe.

steps.title: Unpack and configure
steps.body: Extract into a new folder and run Start.cmd on Windows or ./start.sh on Linux. Warden’s first-run wizard creates server.jsonc with your server name, visibility and public endpoints.

steps.title: Configure your license
steps.body: Supply your license in setup, or keep it in OP77_LICENSE_KEY when configuring the server manually. The master URL defaults to https://master.open2077.net/.

steps.title: Run it
steps.body: Open the game and resource-download ports, then start the configured server. Public servers register with the master so players can discover and join them.

start.notice: Open the game and resource-download ports in your firewall, keep your license key out of scripts and screenshots, and protect your Warden access. The <guide>hosting guide</guide> covers all of it before you invite players.

items.title: The game is not needed
items.body: A dedicated server runs independently of Cyberpunk 2077, REDengine and the client plugin. It never loads game content and never needs a copy installed.

items.title: Windows x64 or Linux x64
items.body: Both official packages include the .NET runtime and native networking dependencies. No separate .NET installation on the host; the <guide>setup guide</guide> lists the OS-level prerequisites.

items.title: Your players still need the game
items.body: Everyone who connects needs {requirement} on their own machine and a free OPEN//77 account. No access application is needed.

faq.q: Do I need approval to host a server?
faq.a: No. Open Alpha server downloads are public, with no sign-in or approval required. Create a free OPEN//77 account and verify your email to generate a server license key. No developer application or staff role is needed.

Downloads are public. If the release service is temporarily unavailable, refresh this page or check the <status>service status</status>. You do not need an account or an access grant to see the archives.

faq.q: Where does the license key go?
faq.a: Supply it in Warden’s first-run setup, or keep it in OP77_LICENSE_KEY when configuring the server by hand. The licensing guide covers activation. Never paste keys into public scripts or screenshots.

faq.q: How do I update an existing server?
faq.a: Read the release notes, back up your configuration, resources and data, then stop the server before unpacking the new archive over it. Check client/server compatibility and test your own resources before reopening.

ncwe.metaTitle: NCWE {version}, the Night City World Editor
ncwe.metaDescription: Download NCWE Studio {version}, the stable world editor for Cyberpunk 2077. Edit Night City, build with roads, terrain, lights and your own models, and export ArchiveXL mods or OPEN//77 multiplayer worlds. Free, no account needed.
title: Shape
Night City
as you want.
ncwe.lead: NCWE is the free world editor for Cyberpunk 2077. Fly through the real city, move or remove what is there, build new places with roads, terrain, lights and your own models, then ship them as an ArchiveXL mod or an OPEN//77 multiplayer world.
ncwe.heroNote: Windows 10 and 11 · Cyberpunk 2077 {game} · no account needed

title: Night City, live
around your camera.
city.lead: Not a blank grid and not a copy: the editor reads the city from your own game and draws it as you fly, so what you build sits in the real streets from the first click.

points.title: It streams as the game does.
points.body: No neighborhood to load: sectors arrive around your camera the way the game picks them, and a place you have visited comes back almost at once.

points.title: It looks like the game.
points.body: Near the camera, meshes wear their real materials: layered surfaces, glass, decals, water, neons, screens and foliage, under a sun, a sky and a night preview.

points.title: It leaves your game alone.
points.body: A project is a list of changes against the game's data. Nothing in your installation is rewritten, and every export is checked against what you edited.

title: Everything a mapper
reaches for.
tools.lead: One editor for the whole job: change what the game put there, then add what it never had.

items.title: Move what is there
items.body: Select, move, rotate, scale, hide or replace the game's own objects, with gizmos, snapping and unlimited undo.

items.title: Roads
items.body: Draw splines with any game road type, bank them, drop them on the ground. They export with collision that follows the surface.

items.title: Terrain
items.body: Sculpt, cut and paint the ground. Plants and the objects resting on it follow.

items.title: Lights, effects, decals, sounds
items.body: Place point, spot and area lights, particles, decals and sound emitters, or edit the game's own.

items.title: Doors and entities
items.body: Place any entity template, pick its appearance, and set how a door opens, closes and locks.

items.title: Elevators
items.body: Pick a type, click each floor it stops at. It exports as the game builds its own, with call panels and landing doors.

items.title: Collision and occlusion
items.body: See the game's real collision and occluders, edit them, add your own, or fit collision to a mesh.

items.title: Traffic
items.body: View, edit, link and draw the lanes vehicles and pedestrians follow.

items.title: Library and prefabs
items.body: Browse the game's props and entities with thumbnails and live 3D previews. Save your own prefabs and stamp them anywhere.

title: Bring what the game
never shipped.
content.lead: Your library lives beside the game's. What a world uses travels with it when you export or share it.

items.title: Your meshes
items.body: Import glTF, FBX or OBJ. NCWE cooks them into game meshes and textures when you export.

items.title: Your decals
items.body: Any picture becomes a decal, transparency kept. Keep them in a bank and place them like the game's.

items.title: Your sounds
items.body: Ambiences and music for OPEN//77 worlds. A synced loop plays at the same moment for every player.

together.title: Build with your crew.

items.title: Live sessions.
items.body: Everyone's edits arrive as they are made; you see the others' cameras and selections, with chat built in.

items.title: Shared worlds.
items.body: Share a world with an invite code: one builds at night, another goes on in the morning.

items.title: Cloud saves.
items.body: Every version of your worlds, on any PC, with the models and sounds they use.

together.note: These three use a free OPEN//77 account. Building alone never does.

agents.title: Or hand the tools to an agent.

items.title: An MCP server comes with it.
items.body: Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client drives the running editor.

items.title: You watch it work.
items.body: The agent says what it plans, measures in your view, and every batch is one undo step.

items.title: Same tools as you.
items.body: Interiors, streets and new places, built with what the editor already does.

agents.note: The automation pipe is local and limited to your Windows user.

title: From the editor
to the game.
ship.lead: One project, three ways out. Each export carries a manifest of what it changes and what it was built against.

items.title: ArchiveXL mod
items.body: A package for archive/pc/mod with its own sectors and guarded patches. Install it and remove it from the editor.

items.title: OPEN//77 world
items.body: A server resource the launcher installs for every player before the game starts. Your map, on your server.

items.title: World Builder
items.body: A file for WolvenKit's World Builder, to carry what you placed into that workflow.

title: Get
NCWE.
download.text: Free, no account, nothing else to install: .NET and the Windows App SDK come in the zip.
download.copySha: Copy the SHA-256 of the download

steps.title: Download and extract
steps.body: Unzip the whole archive into a folder of your choice. Do not start NCWE from inside the zip.

steps.title: Start NCWE.Studio.exe
steps.body: The release is not signed yet: if Windows SmartScreen appears, choose More info, then Run anyway.

steps.title: Open Night City
steps.body: NCWE finds your Cyberpunk 2077 installation on its own, or asks for its folder. Then fly.

items.a: Yes. NCWE is free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0. No game data is included: it reads the city from your own installation.
Not to build. An OPEN//77 account is only asked for cloud saves and live collaboration, and signing in happens on open2077.net in your browser.

Cyberpunk 2077 {game}, on Windows 10 or 11 with a DirectX 11 graphics card. To play what you export, the game needs ArchiveXL and RED4ext. Install <archivexl>our build of ArchiveXL 1.28</archivexl> ({archivexlVersion}): the official 1.28.0 crashes on deleted game objects and keeps their collision. Source on <source>GitHub</source>.

items.q: Will it change my game files?
items.a: No. Projects are stored as changes, and an export is a separate mod you install and remove. Your vanilla files are never rewritten.

items.q: How do I update from the beta?
items.a: Close NCWE, download the stable release and extract it to a new folder. Start NCWE.Studio.exe from that folder. Your settings and sign-in are kept, and your projects stay where you saved them.

items.q: Where can I report a problem?
items.a: Help > Open the logs folder collects what we need for a bug report. Bring the logs and the steps to reproduce the problem to the OPEN//77 Discord.

ncwe.thanks: NCWE stands on <wolvenkit>WolvenKit</wolvenkit> and <archivexl>ArchiveXL</archivexl>. Without them it would not exist: thank you to their authors.
ncwe.fineprint: NCWE is free software (GPL-3.0). It is an independent community project, unaffiliated with CD PROJEKT RED; Cyberpunk 2077 is a trademark of CD PROJEKT S.A. No game data is included.

title: The network.
At a glance.
hero.lead: Live service health, measured availability and a transparent record of every interruption, straight from the monitor.

alerts.errorTitle: The monitoring feed could not be refreshed.
alerts.staleBody: The last recorded history remains below. Old checks are not treated as current health.
alerts.errorBody: This does not establish whether services are up or down. Please retry shortly.
alerts.noscript: JavaScript is required for live updates. The <feed>public JSON feed</feed> is available without JavaScript.

services.title: Platform services
services.waiting: Waiting for monitoring data. Availability history will appear here once collection is active.

bars.group: {name}: {days}-day availability, select a day for details

latency.title: Every millisecond counts.
latency.note: End-to-end check duration, not in-game ping. CDN checks include release metadata and 4 KiB partial downloads. Missing samples are never joined across gaps.
latency.chartTitle: {service} response time over 24 hours. {count} measured five-minute buckets. Gaps mean no successful checks.
latency.caption: Five-minute average check times, UTC, latest first

maintenance.title: Heads up.
maintenance.noneBody: No active or upcoming maintenance in the latest feed.

incidents.title: The record, not the guesswork.
incidents.nothingBody: No confirmed incidents recorded in the observed period.
incidents.unavailableBody: Incident history is unavailable until the monitor responds.
incidents.rules: Incidents open after two consecutive failed checks and close after two successful checks. Single failures still appear in availability. Detection is not a root-cause diagnosis.

method.source: Measurements come from {region}. A check runs every minute. This is a single monitoring vantage point, not a global service-level guarantee. Community game servers and end-to-end sign-in are not covered.
method.formula: Availability = successful checks ÷ completed checks. Slow but successful responses remain available. Coverage = completed checks ÷ scheduled minute slots in the selected UTC calendar days. Unobserved periods, including before monitoring began, are unknown — never counted as uptime. Maintenance does not erase failed checks.
method.bars: Daily bars show the worst observed result; stripes indicate incomplete coverage. The response graph averages successful checks in five-minute buckets. Data older than three minutes becomes unknown, even if the last result was healthy.
method.notStarted: Collection start is not yet known.
method.retention: History is retained for 90 days. A monitor or network outage may prevent observations; incident timestamps do not prove uninterrupted downtime between checks.

footer.fineprint: Status reflects automated checks from the stated monitoring location, not a guarantee of availability from every network.

launcher.metaDescription: Sign in to connect the OPEN//77 launcher on your device to your platform account.

title: Your
account
account.lead: One account for the whole platform: the server browser, your game identities, your Workshop creations, and the license keys your servers run on.

title: Lost your
password?
forgot.lead: It happens. We'll e-mail you a single-use link to choose a new one.
notes: Use the latest e-mail: links are single-use and expire after a short while.
Keep the link to yourself. Nobody from OPEN//77 will ever ask you for it.

title: New
password
reset.lead: You followed a reset link from your inbox. Choose the new password for your account and sign in with it.
notes: Use the latest e-mail: links are single-use and expire after a short while.
Keep the link to yourself. Nobody from OPEN//77 will ever ask you for it.

title: Verify your
e-mail
verify.lead: One click and your address is confirmed. Verification is required before you can create server license keys.
notes: Use the latest e-mail: links are single-use and expire after a short while.

title: Authorize
launcher
launcher.lead: Connect the OPEN//77 launcher running on this device to your platform account. The launcher never sees your password.
notes: Approve only what you started: if you did not open this page from the launcher, close it.
The launcher receives a short-lived code. Your password never leaves this page.

title: Connect
GitHub
github.lead: Verify your public identity and import release assets into the Workshop, without granting write access to your repositories.
notes: Approve only what you started: if you did not open this page from GitHub, close it.
Read access to your public identity and releases. No write permissions.

title: Approve
Warden
warden.lead: Let your server's Warden prepare Workshop resource drafts under your account. Review exactly what it asks for before you approve it.
notes: Approve only what you started: if you did not open this page from your Warden, close it.
A scoped token for the project you pick, revocable from your account.

footnote.alpha: Create a free account to play and host. Open Alpha needs no access approval.
footnote.master: Accounts run against the OPEN//77 master server.
